mathematical_repair_assessment.subject: lem-finite-cellular-nonzero-form-heads-purity-and-shared-factor-linkage
mathematical_repair_assessment.independent_argument: For empty T the cell space, Gram form and layer are zero, hence block support and simple factors are empty and its corner summands vanish. For nonempty T, equality B tensor I = I tensor A forces each central idempotent to act as a scalar; orthogonality and sum1 select exactly one block, regardless of vanishing Gram form. Nonzero Gram form gives rank-one actions, unique maximal radical and absolute simple quotient. Finite maximal ideal support exhausts simples and supports multiplicity triangularity. Head pairing is symmetric associative and nondegenerate, so star dual preserves each simple label; exact primitive projections on cell layers give the corner identity. Nonnegative products in that identity equate primitive graph edges with shared factors of genuine nonzero cells. Every nonzero finite cell has a simple factor, so connected nonzero-cell chains recover blocks; zero cells supply no vertex. This validates the minimal nonzero-chain restriction and explicit empty-support convention without removing any rich nonzero result.
mathematical_repair_assessment.consumer_route: Schur standards have canonical unit Gram entries, and Spechts have standard-tableau bases, so actual Schur and Hecke cells used for block linkage are nonzero. Head-classification/generic semisimplicity/primitive-content consumers only use unchanged nonzero-head clauses. Jantzen descendants concern actual nonzero standards. Remaining descendants transport these preserved conclusions; no Statement/Definition consumer changes required.

[F1] Standard block purity, shared-simple-factor linkage, the unitriangular
standard $K_0$ basis, and the Schur/Specht block correspondence: two standards
$\Delta^\lambda,\Delta^\mu$ share a block exactly when the corresponding
Murphy Specht modules $S^\lambda,S^\mu$ share a block, and cell modules share
a block exactly when linked by a finite chain of cell modules whose
neighbouring terms share a simple factor
([[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]]).

3.1 Blocks and Hecke linkage. By [F1], two standards share a Schur block exactly when they are linked by a finite chain of standards whose neighbouring terms share a simple factor. Step 2.2 converts each such shared factor into a $J$-edge to the common index, and step 2.1 shows every $J$-edge lies inside one block; hence sharing a Schur block is equivalent to $\sim_J$-connectivity. Applying the established Schur/Specht block correspondence of [F1] transfers this equivalence to the Murphy Specht modules and the Hecke algebra. In rank $0$ there is one empty standard, all positive filtration terms vanish, and the single empty class is its own Jantzen class; the argument never reduces $J$ coefficients modulo the field characteristic. [F1, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎
